summary: The session discusses the integration of AI agents into existing data analytics teams, emphasizing the need for a shift in operating models to focus on business outcomes rather than traditional reporting metrics. It highlights real-world examples of organizations successfully adopting AI agents and outlines three key steps: facilitating a new delivery model, developing necessary skills, and establishing governance frameworks. The speaker advocates for a product-centric approach to AI implementation, ensuring that human oversight remains integral to the process.

key_points: AI agents are likened to historical technological advancements that faced initial skepticism.
Many organizations struggle to implement AI effectively due to outdated operating models.
An outcome-based delivery model is essential for effectively integrating AI agents.
Collaboration between business and analytics teams is crucial for achieving desired outcomes.
New roles, such as AI product managers, are necessary to guide AI integration.
Documenting existing workflows is vital for aligning analytics with business outcomes.
Establishing trust in AI outputs is critical due to potential inaccuracies.
Organizations must balance innovation with safety and complexity in AI governance.

key_takeaways: Shift your data analytics operating model to focus on business outcomes rather than just reporting metrics.
Develop new skills and roles within your team to effectively collaborate with AI agents.
Establish governance frameworks that prioritize trust and accountability in AI outputs.
